articles.title: Rohit Sharma scripts history in 3rd ODI, becomes fastest batter to reach 10000 runs as opener
articles.summary: The West Indies series has already been a memorable one for Rohit Sharma.
articles.body: The West Indies series has already been a memorable one for Rohit Sharma. After scoring a century in the second ODI and completing 12,000 ODI runs, the Indian opener added another milestone to his name in the third and final ODI at Mullanpur.With India already holding an unassailable 2-0 lead, captain Shubman Gill opted to bat first after winning the toss. Rohit quickly reached another landmark, becoming only the fourth batter in ODI history to score 10,000 runs as an opener.Rohit reached the milestone in just 202 innings, making him the fastest batter to 10,000 ODI runs as an opener. He joined an elite list featuring Sachin Tendulkar (15,310), Sanath Jayasuriya (12,740) and Chris Gayle (10,179).Seales strikes twice as Gill, Kohli depart cheaplyIndia, however, endured a difficult start after losing two quick wickets. Gill was dismissed for just one before Virat Kohli followed him back to the pavilion for a golden duck.Jayden Seales struck twice in quick succession. Gill was caught by Shai Hope down the leg side in the third over, before Kohli was bowled through the gate by Seales on the very next delivery. Ruturaj Gaikwad then joined Rohit in the middle as India looked to rebuild after losing two quick wickets.Playing Xis For India vs West Indies 3rd ODIIndia (Playing XI): Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill(c), Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, KL Rahul(w), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj, Gurnoor BrarWest Indies (Playing XI): John Campbell, Jewel Andrew, Shai Hope(w/c), Amir Jangoo, Sherfane Rutherford, Keemo Paul, Matthew Forde, Alzarri Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Jayden Seales, Vitel LawesStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shai Hope battles cramps as West Indies chase down 352 to register five-wicket win over India in third ODI
articles.summary: New Chandigarh: India’s ODI team is in a phase where it is on the lookout for stern challenges to identify its own core group for the World Cup in South
articles.body: New Chandigarh: India’s ODI team is in a phase where it is on the lookout for stern challenges to identify its own core group for the World Cup in South Africa, which is a year away. After two lopsided victories in the first two ODIs, India were finally tested by West Indies for the entire length of the match, which ended with captain Shai Hope’s effortless unbeaten 162 off 143 balls chasing down 352-run target with 10 balls and five wickets remaining.Coming out to open the batting, Hope overshadowed KL Rahul’s counterattacking unbeaten 129 off 87 balls that propelled India to 351/7. Dew may have played a part, but Hope’s experience tamed down India’s inexperienced bowling with consummate ease as the West Indies team pulled one back in the series to soothe the pain of the impending pay cuts in their match fees.India’s greatest challenge coming into the series was to identify a backup pace attack to complement Jasprit Bumrah. The team management may have to wait a little longer to nail the pace attack.Be it the pace and movement up front in the match or Hope’s unwavering temperament in the chase, India were always playing catch-up. When Jayden Seales breached Virat Kohli’s defence immediately after removing Shubman Gill off the previous ball in the third over of the match, the conditions seemed like what one may expect in South Africa in a year’s time. If ever the selectors needed an affirmation about Rohit Sharma’s capability to survive and dominate in testing conditions, his carefully paced knock of 92 off 85 to put India back on track did just that.After the first 10 overs of the match, where India laboured to 32/2, Rohit broke free along with Ruturaj Gaikwad to resume the usual business of brisk run-scoring. India kept losing wickets at regular intervals, but the scoring rate maintained an upward trajectory till they finished with 351/7.As has been the trend in the series, run scoring never looked challenging for the batters. Just like India cruised to victory while chasing big totals in the previous two games, West Indies batters too looked fairly untroubled in the evening. The only thing that troubled Hope was running between the wickets with cramps. Had Amir Jangoo not been run out for 67 off 56, things would have moved at a faster rate for West Indies.Rahul’s innings did have a couple of dropped catches in it, but his fluency was such that one couldn’t make out this was his only outing with the bat in the series. Rahul faces stiff competition from Ishan Kishan for holding on to his spot in the XI. Saturday’s knock will improve his stocks as the lead wicketkeeper in the team.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India T20 team beat Pakistan to win Asian Games - but ODI side miss out on series sweep of West Indies after Shai Hope's 162 not out
articles.summary: Shai Hope's unbeaten ton leads West Indies to their record chase of 352 and denies India 3-0 ODI sweep; Windies captain on field for every ball of match in New Chandigarh; earlier in Japan, India's T20 team beat Pakistan for seventh time in a row in the format to win Asian Games gold
articles.body:
In the Asian Games final in Japan, India smoked 211-6 from their 20 overs, underpinned by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 balls, Tilak Varma's 51 not out from 22 and Shivam Dube's 27 off 15.

Pakistan plummeted to 39-3 in reply and despite Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, they could muster only 192-6 and lost by 19 runs.

The victory was India's seventh in a row over fierce rivals Pakistan in T20Is and their 14th in the 18 matches between the teams in the format.

Tireless Hope hits brilliant ton as India denied ODI sweep

In New Chandigarh, however, India saw their total of 351-7 eclipsed by West Indies with 10 balls to spare as visiting captain Hope struck his 21st ODI hundred and second in as many matches to secure a five-wicket win after defeats in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.

Hope's 143-ball knock featured 17 fours and and three sixes, with his final maximum, a slog sweep over deep fine leg off spinner Naman Dhir, bringing the scores level before he drove the match-clinching single to long-off.

There was a controversial moment when Sherfane Rutherford was given out caught behind off Dhir for 24, with the on-field decision upheld after a review despite the West Indies batter feeling the spike on Snicko was bat on pad, not bat on ball.

Rutherford's dismissal left West Indies 206-3 after 30 overs but Hope - who kept for 50 overs and then opened the battings - shared half-century stands with Keemo Paul (44) and Gudakesh Motie (19), having earlier put on 109 with Amir Jangoo (67).

India's score, achieved after they had tumbled to 4-2, was based on KL Rahul's 129 not out off 87 balls, plus Rohit Sharma's 92 from 85 deliveries and Ruturaj Gaikkwad's 57 off 69.

Shubman Gill (1) - who hit an unbeaten 223 in the second ODI as India chased down 406 to take an unassailable 2-0 lead - and Virat Kohli (0) fell to successive balls from Jayden Seales in the third over.

Kohli was bowled for a golden duck as Seales flattened his middle stump, moments after Gill had edged behind and been dismissed by a one-handed diving catch from Hope.

The teams will now meet in five T20s, starting in Lucknow on Tuesday, with Abhishek, Tilak, Shreyas Iyer and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the players to fly in for that series following victory at the Asian Games.

Cricket has been part of the Asian Games at every edition since 2010, bar the 2018 event in Indonesia, with India claiming gold on their competition debut in China in 2022 before backing up that success in Japan this year.

The next Asian Games is due to be held in Qatar in November 2030.

articles.title: 'Doing things for social media': Former Pakistan player slams Saim Ayub for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi send-off
articles.summary: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games men’s cricket final on Saturday, but the match was much closer than the final score suggests.
articles.body: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games men’s cricket final on Saturday, but the match was much closer than the final score suggests. Pakistan, led by Sahibzada Farhan, pushed India hard, with Hasan Nawaz scoring 96.India eventually held its nerve in the final overs through Jasprit Bumrah and Shivam Dube to retain the gold medal.The match also saw controversy when Pakistan all-rounder Saim Ayub dismissed 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 15 off nine balls.After taking the wicket, Ayub appeared to make a ‘baby cradle’ gesture, which was seen as a send-off directed at the young Indian batter. Sooryavanshi did not react and simply returned to the dugout.Kamran Akmal criticises Saim AyubFormer Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Kamran Akmal criticised Ayub’s celebration during a discussion on the ‘Game Plan’ YouTube show.The presenter questioned the gesture and said, “Did you see that action? How unfortunate is that? You are playing such good cricket. You are giving India competition after such a long time. These things don't look good.”Akmal agreed with the criticism and said, “These things have been happening for a long time. Our performance hasn't been great, but we are doing things for social media. The management should think about this. It's international cricket. No matter whether he is 13, 14 or 15, he's playing international cricket. Saim Ayub is not a kid. He should focus on his performances.”Sooryavanshi made a quick startSooryavanshi had started aggressively, hitting Saad Masood for two sixes in the second over. However, his attempt to play a reverse sweep against Ayub ended his innings.India posted 211/6, with Abhishek Sharma scoring 61, Tilak Varma making an unbeaten 51 and Shivam Dube contributing 27. Pakistan fought back through Hasan Nawaz and Ayub, but India pulled away in the final two overs.Dube played a key role as India secured a 19-run victory and successfully defended its Asian Games title.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Great man MS Dhoni’: Shai Hope reveals advice from ex-India captain that helped him script record chase
articles.summary: Shai Hope turned to advice from former India captain MS Dhoni to pace his innings as West Indies chased down their highest-ever ODI target against India
articles.body: Shai Hope turned to advice from former India captain MS Dhoni to pace his innings as West Indies chased down their highest-ever ODI target against India and signed off the series with a five-wicket win on Saturday.Hope produced an unbeaten 162 off 143 balls, his second successive century in the series, to guide West Indies to 352-5 in 48.2 overs after India posted 351-7. The visitors completed the chase with 10 balls to spare, ending India's winning streak in the series after defeats in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Hope revealed that a conversation with Dhoni had influenced the way he approached the chase."Something that I had a great chat with the great man MS Dhoni, he was telling you always have more time than you think," Hope said."Just trying not to focus too much on the end result. Just look at the process, try to break the game down as best as I can and find ways to get the boundaries in the back end."The advice proved particularly valuable given the circumstances. Hope had promoted himself to opener after Jewel Andrew reportedly injured a finger while taking a catch and was taken to hospital. He had also spent the entire 50 overs behind the stumps in high humidity before walking out to bat.West Indies were also a batter short, while Hope said the team could effectively have been two down with Vitel Lawes unavailable."It would always be a challenge," Hope said. "So just trying not to focus too much on the end result."Hope reached his 50 off 46 balls and brought up his 21st ODI hundred from 104 deliveries. He then shifted gears dramatically, scoring 62 runs from his final 39 balls.After Keemo Paul fell in the 41st over, Hope added 62 off 29 balls with Gudakesh Motie to take West Indies over the line. India's slow over rate meant the hosts had to have an additional fielder inside the 30-yard circle for the final four overs, something Hope had anticipated."I even thought about the overs that the Indian team were behind. So I knew they would have to bring a couple fielders in, in the back end," he said."It's always tough when you're trying to defend a score and you got to have five men in the ring. So all those things I calculated when I was batting. Just so happened that everything worked out for us in the back end."Hope also revealed that he began feeling discomfort around his groin after about 30 overs of the chase but decided to push through."Probably about 30 overs in, felt a little something in the groin area. So just tried to fight to the end there," he said.He fittingly struck the winning run, completing a remarkable chase that gave West Indies their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket.India's total had been built around KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 off 87 balls, while Rohit Sharma made 92. But Hope's marathon effort ensured West Indies finally had something to celebrate after India had already sealed the three-match series with two convincing wins.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill equals MS Dhoni, Yuvraj Singh to enter elite India club
articles.summary: Shubman Gill continued to strengthen his credentials as one of India's most consistent performers in ODI cricket, equalling MS Dhoni's tally of seven
articles.body: Shubman Gill continued to strengthen his credentials as one of India's most consistent performers in ODI cricket, equalling MS Dhoni's tally of seven Player of the Series awards after India's three-match series against the West Indies on Saturday.Gill's latest recognition came despite India losing the third ODI by five wickets, with the hosts winning the series 2-1. The Indian captain scored a century in the opening match and followed it up with a double hundred in the second, both innings coming while chasing.Gill struck 110 in the first ODI before producing a stunning unbeaten 233 in the second. His performances helped India secure the series before the West Indies bounced back with a record chase in the final match.With seven Player of the Series awards, Gill has now drawn level with Dhoni among Indian players. He also matches Yuvraj Singh and Sourav Ganguly, while Virat Kohli has 11 such awards and Sachin Tendulkar leads the list with 15.What makes Gill's record particularly striking is the period in which he has achieved it. All seven of his Player of the Series awards have come since 2022. No other Indian player has won more than three in the same period, underlining his consistency across bilateral ODI contests.The West Indies, however, ensured India did not complete a clean sweep. Shai Hope's unbeaten 162 powered the visitors to 352 for five, their highest successful ODI chase, after India posted 351 for seven.KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 and Rohit Sharma's 92 had put India in a commanding position, but Hope's masterclass secured a consolation victory for the visitors.India nevertheless took the series 2-1, with Gill's remarkable run across the first two matches earning him another individual milestone and drawing him level with one of India's most celebrated former captains.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies ODI series rewrites record books with highest scoring rate ever
articles.summary: The India-West Indies ODI series was a run-fest from start to finish, with the three-match contest setting a new record for the highest scoring rate in a
articles.body: The India-West Indies ODI series was a run-fest from start to finish, with the three-match contest setting a new record for the highest scoring rate in a bilateral series involving at least three ODIs.The series recorded a scoring rate of 7.43 runs per over, the highest in the format for a bilateral series of three or more matches.The previous record was held by England's 2015 home series against New Zealand, which produced a scoring rate of 7.15 runs per over. India themselves were involved in the third-highest mark, scoring at 7.00 runs per over against England in the 2017 series. England's 2019 series against Pakistan comes fourth at 6.97.The numbers underline just how explosive the India-West Indies contest was.The first ODI saw 595 runs scored, with West Indies making 295 for seven before India chased down the target in just 41.4 overs, finishing on 300 for two.The second ODI raised the bar considerably. West Indies piled up 405 for seven, only for India to chase down the target in 43.3 overs, reaching 406 for two. The match produced 811 runs.The run-scoring continued in the series finale, with India making 351 for seven before West Indies completed a record chase of 352 for five in 48.2 overs. The third ODI alone produced 703 runs.Across the three matches, both teams repeatedly crossed the 300-run mark. India eventually won the series 2-1, sealing victories by eight wickets in the first two matches before West Indies produced a five-wicket consolation win in the finale.The series was so heavily tilted towards the batters that, apart from Kuldeep Yadav's four-wicket spell in the opening ODI, there was little in the bowling departments to remember. The India spinner's spell stood out as one of the few occasions when a bowler managed to exert sustained influence on a contest otherwise dominated by the bat.Even India's 406-run chase in the second ODI prompted head coach Gautam Gambhir to question whether such batting-friendly conditions offered enough preparation for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Gambhir was unequivocal in his assessment after the match."There has to be a bit more contest between bat and ball because this is not cricket, this is only batting," he said.His comments pointed to a larger concern for India despite their 2-1 series win. While the extraordinary scoring rates made for compelling batting numbers, the series also exposed questions around India's bowling attack.Kuldeep was the notable exception, with his four-wicket haul in the first ODI providing one of the few standout bowling performances of the series. Beyond him, India struggled to consistently make an impact with the ball across the three matches.Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel are expected to return to the ODI setup, which should strengthen the attack, but the series has nevertheless left India with questions over the depth and balance of their bowling options ahead of the 2027 World Cup.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shai Hope's 162 breaks Tillakaratne Dilshan's 17-year-old record in historic chase against India
articles.summary: Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 against India in the third ODI at New Chandigarh may have looked like another masterclass from the West Indies captain, but the
articles.body: Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 against India in the third ODI at New Chandigarh may have looked like another masterclass from the West Indies captain, but the innings was anything but ordinary.Hope produced a record-breaking knock to guide West Indies to a stunning five-wicket victory while chasing 352, their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket. In the process, the right-hander broke Tillakaratne Dilshan’s long-standing record for the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase against India. Hope’s 162 not out, scored off 143 balls with 17 fours and three sixes, surpassed Dilshan’s 160 against India in Rajkot in 2009.Highest scores in a run chase vs India (ODI)162*S Hope New Chandigarh 2026160 T Dilshan Rajkot 2009158 A Strauss Bengaluru 2011151*S Jayasuriya Wankhede 1997It also took him level with Chris Gayle for the highest individual score by a West Indies batter in a successful ODI run chase.Highest scores in a run chase for WI (ODI)162*S Hope vs Ind New Chandigarh 2026162 C Gayle vs Eng St George’s 2019153 B Lara vs Pak Sharjah 1993149*S Chanderpaul vs Ind Nagpur 2007West Indies complete their biggest-ever ODI chaseThe magnitude of Hope’s innings becomes even clearer when viewed alongside the team record. India had posted a daunting 351/7 after opting to bat first, with KL Rahul producing an unbeaten 129 off 87 balls. Rohit Sharma narrowly missed out on a century, scoring 92, while Ruturaj Gaikwad added 57.Despite losing Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli cheaply, India recovered strongly. Gill fell for one and Kohli was dismissed for a golden duck by Jayden Seales, but Rohit and Gaikwad steadied the innings before Rahul provided the late acceleration.West Indies, however, never allowed the asking rate to dictate the chase.John Campbell and Hope raced away at the start before Campbell was dismissed by Mohammed Siraj. Amir Jangoo then joined Hope and the pair put West Indies firmly in control.Jangoo scored a valuable 67, while his partnership with Hope crossed the hundred-run mark. West Indies reached 148/1 at the end of 20 overs and continued to remain ahead of the required rate. Jangoo eventually departed, but Hope remained the constant throughout.The captain had to dig deep late in the innings after beginning to feel discomfort around his groin. He also had to shoulder even more responsibility because Jewel Andrew was unavailable to bat after suffering an injury.Hope briefly went into survival mode, taking 44 balls to move from 87 to 126 without finding the boundary. But once the final phase arrived, he switched gears spectacularly.Alongside Gudakesh Motie, Hope attacked the Indian bowlers and West Indies smashed eight boundaries in just 14 deliveries to take the chase away from India.West Indies eventually reached 352/5 in 48.2 overs, winning with 10 balls to spare.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India withstand Hasan Nawaz onslaught to beat Pakistan, win Asian Games gold
articles.summary: TimesofIndia in Aichi-Nagoya: The warm hugs, high-fives and handshakes that have become a norm between Indian and Pakistani athletes across sports at the
articles.body: TimesofIndia in Aichi-Nagoya: The warm hugs, high-fives and handshakes that have become a norm between Indian and Pakistani athletes across sports at the Asian Games took a leave of absence when the cricket teams played at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Saturday.Enter Shreyas Iyer and his men. There were no customary courtesies, only an expression of rivalry and an unmistakable desire to win gold. By the time the sun set over the Owari Hills, the gold medal was glistening around the necks of Iyer and his men. But Pakistan had ensured it was no procession, launching a late fightback that put the champagne on ice for the defending champions.Opting to bat, India rode on half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma (61; 28b, 3x4, 7x6) and Tilak Varma (51*; 22b, 2x4, 4x6) to post 211/6. Pakistan, reduced to 31/3 at the end of the Powerplay, appeared headed for a heavy defeat. Then Hasan Nawaz took charge, smashing a breathtaking 51-ball 96 (5x4, 7x6). But his assault came too late as Pakistan finished on 192/6, handing India a 19-run victory.On a surface that played differently from the one used in the semifinals, India’s openers took a little time to settle in. Pakistan’s decision to open with off-spinner Saim Ayub looked like a good move but the bubble burst soon after as Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek soon found their range.Sooryavanshi provided the early fireworks, dropping to one knee to launch leg-spinner Saad Masood over the bowler’s head before pulling the next delivery through midwicket. Abhishek was not to be outdone, finding the region beyond mid-on.While Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson returned to the makeshift dressing room, Abhishek, who survived a dropped catch and a run-out, tormented the Pakistan attack as India raced to 81 in the Powerplay.Length was a major issue for Pakistan, who repeatedly bowled short to the in-form batters. Once they got that right, there was a lull of almost six overs without a boundary before Tilak and Shivam Dube launched the late assault.The final push came in the penultimate over, which yielded 23 runs and propelled India beyond 200.With Pakistan 31/3 after six overs, an early finish seemed on the cards. Hasan Nawaz had other ideas. The right-hander produced an innings to remember, keeping Pakistan in the contest almost single-handedly. But by then, India had done enough to ensure the gold stayed with them.For Iyer, the victory was also a reward for a team that had refused to let circumstances derail its campaign.“Ecstatic,” was how he described the feeling. “Since the day we arrived in Japan, it was raining cats and dogs and we couldn’t practise for almost a week. But the boys prepped themselves and we trained on the side. We didn’t complain, we didn’t give any reason,” Iyer said. “That was a sign of a champion team and today was just a reflection of that,” he added.Head coach VVS Laxman said the Asian Games gold carried a special significance for players who had already experienced World Cup success.With cricket returning to the Olympics in 2028, Randy Newman’s super hit song ‘I Love LA’ may well be playing in the players’ mind.Brief scores: India 211-6 (A Sharma 61, Tilak Varma 51 not out, Shivam Dube 27; Arafat Minhas 2-25, Ahmed Daniyal 2-43) beat Pakistan 192-6 in 20 overs (Hasan Nawaz 96, Saim Ayub 29; Axar Patel 2-29, Washington Sundar 2-29) by 19 runs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Manav Suthar named Rajasthan captain for first two Ranji Trophy matches
articles.summary: Jaipur: Promising young talent Manav Suthar, who has made a striking impression at the national level and recently represented India in Test cricket, has
articles.body: Jaipur: Promising young talent Manav Suthar, who has made a striking impression at the national level and recently represented India in Test cricket, has been appointed captain of the Rajasthan team for the opening two matches of the upcoming Ranji Trophy season 2026-27. The announcement was made on Saturday as the senior selection committee named a 15-member squad.Armed with sharp composure, exceptional left-arm spin, and a proven ability to perform under pressure, Manav represents the bright future of Rajasthan cricket. His deputy will be Mahipal Lomror, the team's most experienced batter, providing seasoned guidance in the leadership core.The squad faces significant bowling challenges heading into the initial rounds. Veteran left-arm pacer Aniket Choudhary, long considered the backbone of Rajasthan’s seam attack, will miss the first two fixtures as he recovers from a knee injury. Although he has resumed bowling, he remains below 100% fitness and is slated to return by the third match. This marks the first time in his career that the 36-year-old seamer is missing out on the opening two red-ball games of a domestic season.Adding to the seam department's woes, key bowler Khaleel Ahmed is currently undergoing rehabilitation following an injury sustained during the last IPL. Meanwhile, the absence of premier pacer Deepak Chahar continues to be linked to his reluctance to feature in the longer format of the game.The selected players will gather for a preparatory camp starting Oct 4 at the RCA Academy. Rajasthan kick off their campaign against Tamil Nadu at the Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Stadium from Oct 11, followed by a clash against Railways from Oct 18.Squad (First 2 matches): Manav Suthar (C), Mahipal Lomror (VC), Rohan Rajbar, Sachin Yadav, Sumit Godara, Kartik Sharma, Karan Lamba, Anshul Gadhwal, Mukul Choudhary (WK), Ajay Kookna, Aakash Singh, Chetan Sharma, Hemant Choudhary, Danish Bhamboo, Darshan Jain (WK).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ravichandran Smaran’s unbeaten 126 puts Rest of India in control against J&K in Irani Cup
articles.summary: In red-hot form, Ravichandran Smaran strengthened his case for higher honours with a fighting unbeaten 126 that put Rest of India in control against Jammu
articles.body: In red-hot form, Ravichandran Smaran strengthened his case for higher honours with a fighting unbeaten 126 that put Rest of India in control against Jammu & Kashmir in the Irani Cup at the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium on Saturday.The 23-year-old Karnataka left-hander, recently named his state’s captain for the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, struck 126 not out off 131 balls, with 15 fours and five sixes. It was his seventh first-class century in just his 20th match.RoI were in trouble at 197/8 on Day Three after Akash Deep fell for 1. Earlier, captain Rishabh Pant, who was unwell and walked in at No. 8, was trapped lbw by off-spinner Sahil Lotra for 8, while vice-captain Sarfaraz Khan fell for a rare five-ball duck, caught at slip off Umar Nazir.Smaran then took charge. He added an unbroken 109 for the ninth wicket with No. 10 Mukesh Choudhary, who battled for 47 balls for 9 not out. The stand may yet prove decisive, lifting RoI to 306/8 at stumps and extending their lead to 265.Having top-scored with 68 in the first innings, Smaran again showed the class that brought him 950 runs at 86.36 for Karnataka in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy. He reached his hundred off 113 balls and then smashed 26 off the next 18, attacking the J&K bowlers in fading light.J&K were left to rue repeated lapses. Their bowlers sent down 21 no-balls, with Umar Nazir alone overstepping 15 times in the innings and 22 times in the match. articles.summary: Shoaib Akhtar has dismissed reports linking him with the role of Pakistan’s chief selector, making it clear that he has no interest in taking up any
articles.body: Shoaib Akhtar has dismissed reports linking him with the role of Pakistan’s chief selector, making it clear that he has no interest in taking up any position with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).Speculation around a major overhaul of Pakistan’s coaching and selection setup has intensified since Babar Azam’s side suffered a 0-3 defeat in the three-match Test series against England. Amid the reports of possible changes, Akhtar had been tipped for a key role in the selection committee.However, speaking during a live programme on PTV Sports, the former Pakistan fast bowler rejected the claims.The anchor reminded Akhtar of his earlier comments that his mother had advised him to stay away from the PCB and Pakistani politics. Asked directly about the latest reports, Akhtar said: “There is no such thing, and all that is being said is speculative. I stand by my statement, and I am going to stick to that advice.”“There is no truth to these claims. I am not at all interested in going to the PCB. I stand by my statement. I am hearing all this news about taking on the role of chief selector. This is all fake, and there is no truth to such claims. I just want the betterment of Pakistan cricket,” he added.Akhtar also said he has not held any discussions with the Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB over the reported appointment. The former pacer is currently in Houston on a private visit.‘Many other ways’Despite ruling out any formal association with the PCB, Akhtar said he remains keen to contribute to Pakistan cricket and believes he can do so without taking up an official position.“I would love to serve Pakistan cricket, but I think I can do it in many other ways," Akhtar said.Akhtar, who played 46 Tests, 163 ODIs and 15 T20Is for Pakistan, has remained away from an official role with the board.The reports had earlier claimed that Akhtar met PCB chairman Naqvi for detailed discussions about the national team and ways to improve its fortunes. They also suggested that the relationship between the two had improved in recent months.According to those reports, Naqvi had reached out to Akhtar following the death of the former pacer’s elder brother. articles.title: 'I don’t want to resign': Litton Das rules out stepping down after Bangladesh’s Asian Games failure
articles.summary: Bangladesh captain Litton Das has ruled out stepping down from the leadership role despite his team’s disappointing Asian Games campaign, which ended
articles.body: Bangladesh captain Litton Das has ruled out stepping down from the leadership role despite his team’s disappointing Asian Games campaign, which ended without a medal.Bangladesh suffered a 63-run defeat to Sri Lanka in the bronze-medal playoff, marking the first time they have failed to win a cricket medal at the Asian Games. Sri Lanka, reduced to 21/4 early in their innings, were rescued by Tharindu Ratnayake, whose counter-attacking 65 turned the contest in his team’s favour.Litton admitted Bangladesh failed to perform at their best but credited Ratnayake for producing a match-changing innings.“I think we bowled very well in the first eight overs. Then you saw the kind of shots he played on this wicket. It was very difficult,” Litton told reporters after the match.“He batted extraordinarily and our bowlers had no clue how to come back. Credit has to be given to him for playing such an extraordinary innings. When we went out to bat, we couldn’t cover it up in any way. We were not up to the mark with the bat today,” he added.Litton rules out resignationLitton, who scored just 2 and 0 in Bangladesh’s two matches at the Games, acknowledged that his own performance was below expectations. However, he insisted there was no reason for him to walk away from the captaincy.“My performance was not up to the mark. I could not perform well in both matches,” he said.“I don’t want to resign. There are ups and downs in cricket. One day it will be good and one day it will be bad. There is no point in resigning here. It’s normal. I came with a big target. When I can’t deliver that, everyone will feel bad, and that’s natural.“But as a team, we have given a lot in the past. I think we will give in the future too. We will try for that again,” Litton added.Litton defends players over hotel incidentReports of Bangladesh players leaving the team hotel without informing the authorities also emerged after the defeat, with the incident reportedly leading to the possibility of disciplinary action.Litton, however, defended the players and questioned the facilities available to the team, saying they needed suitable spaces to train as well as access to food that met their requirements.“Practice is required. Are there facilities there? No. So will a player be confined inside a room all day?” Litton said.“They need energy. If you think that the food being provided by the federation or the Asian Games is not suitable for us, then should a player not eat? If they want to eat, they have to go outside. That’s what the players did,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No time to experiment': Captain Shubman Gill wants all resources available for India's ODI World Cup prep
articles.summary: New Chandigarh: If one takes a quick scan of India’s ODI resources for next year’s World Cup in South Africa, the pace cupboard wears a bare and fragile
articles.body: New Chandigarh: If one takes a quick scan of India’s ODI resources for next year’s World Cup in South Africa, the pace cupboard wears a bare and fragile look. There’s only Jasprit Bumrah who truly commands a place in the XI. The rest are either on trial or nursing injuries. Mohammed Siraj has gone off the boil dramatically, losing the confidence of the team management. The other ‘experienced’ pacer in the ranks, Prasidh Krishna, was still in the process of establishing his credentials before breaking down in the second ODI. TOI understands that the team management has identified Gurnoor Brar as a strong prospect in South African conditions.It’s been a rough initiation into ODI captaincy for Shubman Gill. It’s been a year since he assumed the role, but he is yet to get all of his first-choice resources at his disposal. “It’s been unfortunate with the injuries and with the scheduling. We have not been able to play the bowling line-up that we would like to. It’s a great chance for them to showcase their skills,” Gill said after the series win over West Indies here on Saturday.The anxiety was apparent, though. He declared the need for urgency in sorting out the ODI core. With Bumrah away playing in the Asian Games, this series was meant to check the second line of pacers. But Gill doesn’t seem to be in any mood to be in the experimental phase. “I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully we get all the players that are available from the next series. The combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination,” he stated.Here’s the catch. The next series is a five-ODI affair in New Zealand, which will be followed by a two-Test series. Precariously placed in the World Test Championship table, the team management intends to pull out the Test regulars after the third ODI. That would mean Bumrah, Krishna and Siraj will not be available for the entire series. There’s a strong chance Brar, too, could be pulled out.Pace bowling was India’s biggest asset in the last two World Cups. Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Siraj were incisive with the new ball and potent in the death overs. Gill clearly sees the gap in his bowling attack.“Bowling in the power play and in the death have hurt us. If you don’t get off to a good start in the power play, it’s not easy to take wickets in the middle overs. It’s not easy to create chances with only four fielders outside the ring. The intensity of the game is completely different if you don’t keep taking wickets either in the power play or in the middle overs. That’s why this series has been so high scoring. Even today we lost two wickets in the power play but we still managed to get 350 on the board,” Gill spelt out his concerns.Kamboj, Nabi on trial for No. 8 spotIt’s not just about the new-ball bowlers. Gill also revealed that the team management is looking for a pacer who can be a capable batter at No. 8. Recurring injuries to Harshit Rana have compounded Gill’s problems. Which is why Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj were handed debuts in this series.“Anshul and Auqib are going to be in the mix a lot. Anshul is someone who can also bat at No. 8. And that number is very crucial for us. We don’t know who will be fit at the World Cup. And if we want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at No. 8, Anshul can do the job. And even Aqib can bat a bit and do the job. So, we want to see which players can deliver under pressure,” Gill said.Both Kamboj and Nabi endured rough debuts, conceding runs at over nine runs per over. However, this is the only spot where Gill may be willing to bide his time.“They would have liked to have done a much better job. But you know, a little bit harsh on them. It’s not easy to come and to be able to deliver straight away. I hope that they learn from their mistakes and the opportunities that they get,” Gill said.Fielding woesGill also made his displeasure about the fielding standards of the team clear. The Indian team’s fielding has worsened over the last eight months.“We dropped around three or four catches today. I don’t think Shai was dropped but still dropping three or four catches breaks the momentum of the team. Our fielding in the series, I would say, has not been up to the mark. I think in the whole series we dropped around seven catches, if I am not wrong. And even in the field today we gave away, many times in the field we were quite sloppy,” he said.“I think leading up to the World Cup, these are the areas where we definitely need to get better at. We need to be at the peak of our powers, especially when we are in the field. It’s not easy for the bowlers, so the fielders can help a lot. And if the wicket is not helping much for the bowlers and the fielding being substandard, it’s a difficult job for the bowlers,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We did not get the gold on a platter’: Sanju Samson on India’s hard-fought win over Pakistan
articles.summary: India’s Asian Games gold medal did not come easily, according to wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson, who credited the presence of experienced players for
articles.body: India’s Asian Games gold medal did not come easily, according to wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson, who credited the presence of experienced players for helping the team navigate the pressure of a high-stakes final against Pakistan.India beat their arch-rivals by 19 runs on Saturday to successfully defend their men’s cricket gold at the continental showpiece.Samson said the experience within the squad proved crucial, particularly during a tournament where rain had repeatedly disrupted practice and match schedules.“We had a very experienced team. That’s where the experience of experienced players comes in. We knew how to manage our energy, how to keep ourselves motivated and focused even when practices were not happening and matches were not happening,” Samson said after the match.India opted to send their regular T20 contingent to the Asian Games, and Samson felt having the ‘A’ team gave them both the quality and composure required for the occasion.“Bringing the ‘A’ team really helped, and that’s what happened against Pakistan in the final. I think it was a proper game for everyone,” he added.Pakistan kept India under pressureIndia posted 211 for six after half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma, but Pakistan refused to let the final become a one-sided contest.Despite India putting up a formidable total, Pakistan made full use of a good batting surface and kept the chase alive deep into the innings, eventually finishing on 192 for six.Samson said the nature of the contest made India’s gold even more rewarding.“Finally, we got to play a good match. We scored 200 in the first innings and thought the second innings could be difficult for Pakistan, but the wicket was good and they also batted well. Everyone got to see a good final.“We did not get the gold on a platter. We had to really work hard for it. That makes it all the more satisfying, and we are all happy,” he said.Samson acknowledged the significance of an India-Pakistan final on the Asian Games stage, but said the players focused on responding to the demands of the match once play began.“Definitely, it’s a big occasion and a big opportunity for all of us to represent our country in an Asian Games final.“That is what happens before and after the game. articles.title: From 89/3 to 111 all out: Mukesh Kumar, Akash Deep trigger J&K collapse as Rest of India win Irani Cup
articles.summary: India pacers Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep shared nine wickets as Rest of India beat reigning Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir by 167 runs on the
articles.body: India pacers Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep shared nine wickets as Rest of India beat reigning Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir by 167 runs on the fourth day to win the 2026-27 Irani Cup in Srinagar on Sunday.Mukesh returned figures of 6/33 to claim his 11th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket and dismantle the Jammu and Kashmir batting line-up. Akash, playing his comeback game, supported his Bengal teammate with 3/25 as J&K, chasing 279, were bowled out for 111.The bowling effort completed a win that had been set up by Ravichandran Smaran, who scored 68 in the first innings and 135 in the second. Smaran helped Rest of India recover from difficult positions in both innings as they went on to win despite conceding a 41-run first-innings lead.Jammu and Kashmir needed only to hold on for a draw to lift the trophy because of their first-innings lead. They appeared to be on course for a favourable result after openers Shubham Khajuria and Qamran Iqbal put together 54 runs for the first wicket.Akash broke the partnership by trapping Iqbal lbw in front of the wicket. Mukesh then struck twice just before lunch, dismissing Shubham Pundir and captain Paras Dogra off successive deliveries in the 15th over.Dogra was bowled after the delivery moved away just enough to beat his defence and hit the middle stump.J&K went into lunch at 89/3 after 19 overs, with Khajuria on 36 and Abdul Samad on six.Khajuria was dismissed by Akash with the first ball after lunch, triggering a collapse. J&K lost their next six wickets for just 22 runs over the following nine overs.Mukesh finished with 6/33, while Akash took 3/25. Akash's workload in the match, which included six wickets across 23.3 overs, will please the national management ahead of India's upcoming tour of New Zealand, with the pacer now appearing to have recovered well enough to be considered for selection.Earlier, Rest of India, who resumed their second innings at 306/8, were bowled out for 319. Umar Nazir, Sunil Kumar and Sahil Lotra took three wickets each for J&K.Brief scores: Rest of India: 237 and 319 beat Jammu and Kashmir: 278 and 111 all out in 28.4 overs (Shubham Khajuria 36; Mukesh Kumar 6/33, Akash Deep 3/25) by 167 runs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Sunil Gavaskar was disappointed to see Rohit Sharma miss out on an ODI century in the third match against the West Indies, saying he wants the Indian
articles.body: Sunil Gavaskar was disappointed to see Rohit Sharma miss out on an ODI century in the third match against the West Indies, saying he wants the Indian opener to finish his international career with more ODI hundreds than his age.Rohit scored 92 off 85 balls, with 10 fours and three sixes, in India’s third ODI against the West Indies. India lost the third ODI after the visitors successfully chased down 352, with captain Shai Hope scoring an unbeaten 162.Rohit had come into the match after scoring a century in the second ODI. With captain Shubman Gill dismissed for one and Virat Kohli out for a golden duck, the ‘Hitman’ once again took responsibility with the bat.Rohit has scored 35 ODI centuries so far. Gavaskar said a 36th hundred in the third ODI would have taken him closer to the milestone he hopes Rohit can achieve before potentially retiring after the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027."The reason I was disappointed with Rohit getting out on 92 is that he didn't get a hundred, and he might possibly quit international cricket after the end of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027. And at that particular point of time, when he decides to call it a day, I personally would like Rohit to have more ODI hundreds than his age. Had he gotten a century in the third ODI, he would have moved closer to achieving that feat with his 36th hundred. For me, it's a special thing when a player's hundreds outnumber his age at retirement. It shows the kind of career they have had and the standard they have kept for so many years. That is why I really want Rohit to reach that mark. In my last year of international cricket, I wanted to get as many Test centuries as my age, and I got out in the 90s thrice. If I'd got those hundreds, then my centuries would have matched the age of my retirement, which was 38," Gavaskar said on JioStar, as quoted by news agency ANI.Gavaskar also pointed out that Rohit’s batting approach has changed since the 2023 ODI World Cup. While Rohit continues to score quickly, he now appears to place more importance on staying at the crease and turning his starts into big scores.According to Gavaskar, that approach can help Rohit score centuries at a good rate while also benefiting India and reducing criticism over slow batting."A slight change has appeared in the batting template of Rohit that he himself set as the captain for the 2023 ODI World Cup, where he was going bang-bang from the first ball, irrespective of the possibility of getting out sooner. Now he recognises that his wicket is valuable. In that 2023 World Cup, he got the team off to great starts, but he's not a batsman who will score just 30-40 runs. He's a hundred-maker! And therefore, I'm happy to see him score big runs. Yes, I know he missed out on a well-deserved ton in this match, but he got a hundred in the previous game. So, the fact that he's recognising that his job as a batter is also to get a hundred, and if he scores big, he gets a hundred in 70-80 deliveries, which is helpful for the team because that is a great scoring rate in a 50-over game and it also keeps him away from the social media critics of slow batting," Gavaskar said.He finished the three-match ODI series against England with 175 runs at an average of 58.33 and a strike rate of 98.31. articles.title: Australia's Marnus Labuschagne hits timely hundred ahead of South Africa Test series, live on Sky Sports from Friday
articles.summary: Steve Smith scores half-century as he warms up for first Test in South Africa since ball-tampering scandal in 2018; Australia playing the Proteas in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town; England to take on South Africa in three Test matches this winter, starting in Johannesburg on December 17
articles.body:
Labuschagne struck 111 from 89 balls, reaching three figures from 76 deliveries and hitting 19 fours, before retiring out against a Cricket South Africa Invitation XI in Potchefstroom.

The 32-year-old will hope to carry that form into the Test arena, starting in Durban this week, having gone 43 innings and over three years without a hundred in the format.

After Labuschagne - who is averaging 25.43 since the 2023 Ashes - made scores of one, 31 and four in the recent 1-1 series draw at home to Bangladesh, ex-Australia captain Ricky Ponting told Sky Sports that the batter's spot in the XI had become "untenable".

However, the Baggy Greens have kept faith with the South Africa-born player and he seems set to line up in his usual No 3 berth at Kingsmead as Australia begin their first Test series in the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Smith scores half-century in Test tune-up

Steve Smith - who along with David Warner and Cameron Bancroft received a ban for the role he played in using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball - Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and Matt Renshaw are the survivors from that contest eight years ago.

Smith, who followed Labuschagne in retiring out, and Renshaw scored 61 and 32 respectively on the second and final day of the tune-up for this month's Tests, while Alex Carey made 57 as Australia replied to the hosts' 318-7 with 368-6.

On day one, Australia used 11 bowlers in order to manage workload with seven taking a wicket apiece and none of the seamers getting through more than 10 overs.

All-rounder Cameron Green did not feature after picking up an abdominal injury in the final ODI against South Africa last week and appears a doubt for the first Test.

After the series opener in Durban, the teams will meet in Gqeberha from October 18 and then Cape Town from October 27.

articles.title: ‘Thanks for the gift’: Rishabh Pant’s 29th birthday made special as Rest of India reclaim Irani Cup
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rishabh Pant could not have asked for a better 29th birthday present.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rishabh Pant could not have asked for a better 29th birthday present. On a day when he missed the action because of fever, the Rest of India captain watched his teammates complete a stunning comeback against Jammu and Kashmir to reclaim the Irani Cup before joining the celebrations with the trophy and cake.Rest of India, after conceding a 41-run first-innings lead to the Ranji Trophy champions, bowled out J&K for just 111 in their chase of 279 on Sunday to seal a commanding 167-run victory at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium.Pant, who made 10 and eight in the match, did not take the field on the fourth day, with Sarfaraz Khan taking over as on-field captain. But his leadership was evident in the way Rest of India responded after falling behind early.‘We just kept on fighting’Addressing his teammates after the victory, Pant said the squad had been driven by the desire to restore pride after going without the Irani Cup for two years.“Guys, great effort. In the last 5-7 days, we were discussing that let's play for the pride and let's play for our monogram. No matter what happens, especially in the first innings, they did a good batting effort and they took the first innings lead,” Pant said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic.“But, in the dressing room, whatever they do, we need to focus on ourselves. Obviously, most of the time, the game went in their favour.”The captain praised his teammates for refusing to let the match slip away.“One thing for sure, our Rest of India team, we didn't let it go. We just kept on fighting with every ounce of intensity we had. One day, one over, one ball at a time and, everyone contributed in their own way,” he said.“From last two years, we were not winning. But, we made sure that when we leave this ground, we put our name on the trophy as winners.”‘Thanks for the gift’The celebrations became even more special with Pant’s birthday falling on the day of the triumph.In a video shared by BCCI Domestic, his teammates and coaches gathered around the wicketkeeper-batter and sang ‘Happy Birthday’ in chorus. Ground staff members also offered their blessings and wishes before Pant cut the cake and posed with the trophy alongside his teammates.“Thanks for the gift,” a smiling Pant said as the dressing-room celebrations continued.The captain also explained how a tactical adjustment in bowling helped turn the contest around.“Mostly the plan was to bowl fuller in the first innings. That was the conversation we had with the bowlers that we were like, we would back up the length,” Pant said at the post-match presentation.“That was something we wanted to correct in the second innings because we knew our bowlers were really good, but the problem was the first innings we bowled too much back of the length, and we corrected that and bowled fuller and fuller in the second innings.”Mukesh Kumar led the demolition with 6-33 as J&K collapsed after lunch.Pant also reserved special praise for young batter Ravichandran Smaran, who scored 68 in the first innings before producing a match-winning 135 in the second.“Today all the pieces fell in place, but at the same time, you know, like you mentioned, Smaran, the way he played in both innings, I think it was outstanding innings, especially we were under pressure, especially in the second innings the way he played, it was outstanding,” Pant said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Clearly, Beckham Jr. wasn't thrilled with the team's decision to release him just weeks after surprising some fans by making him a part of their final 53-man roster ahead of the 2026 season.

Offense has been a major issue for the Giants over the last couple of weeks, ever since starting quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with an injury that forced season-ending surgery.

Since then, the Giants have watched quarterback Jameis Winston struggle to produce in his backup role and have since traded for Minnesota Vikings quarterback JJ McCarthy.

Meanwhile, it remains to be seen whether or not OBJ will get any more opportunities around the league. The former Pro Bowler will turn 34 years old next month and also has a storied injury history, both of which have contributed to his clearly diminished agility and explosiveness on the field.

In any case, the Giants will look to improve to 3-1 on Sunday afternoon at home vs the Arizona Cardinals before hitting the road to take on the Washington Commanders next week.

articles.title: ‘I no longer have the capacity’: England pacer retires after 500-plus wickets, citing mental health
articles.summary: English fast bowler Craig Miles has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 32, saying he needs to step away to protect his
articles.body: English fast bowler Craig Miles has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 32, saying he needs to step away to protect his mental health.Miles, who last played in June during the Vitality Blast, finishes a 15-year career with more than 500 wickets across formats.In an open letter published by Gloucestershire, Miles explained that his recent struggles with cricket had become too difficult to manage."It’s with sadness, but also with huge pride, that I can announce my retirement from professional cricket. Although this has by no means been an easy decision, given the struggles I've experienced with the game in recent times, I've made this call in order to prioritise my mental well-being," he wrote."My recent time away from the game has given me the opportunity to reflect and understand myself better, as well as my relationship with cricket. The challenges I've faced recently are ones I've experienced at other points in my career, although never with the same intensity as this time. The high expectations I place on myself and the standards I've always tried to reach, have often been the catalyst for these periods."At times, they have compromised how I've felt about my abilities and performances. The questioning and self-doubt that follow only serve to reinforce an unhelpful narrative. When you add in the volatility and uncertainty that cricket naturally brings, it becomes an unforgiving and ultimately unsustainable way to approach the game."Looking back on his careerMiles said he no longer felt capable of maintaining the standards he expected from himself, despite having enjoyed many successful periods in the sport."Unfortunately, I now feel I no longer have the capacity to continue in a way that allows me to train, play and perform to a standard I can accept from myself. Of course, there have also been so many periods when I’ve loved the game, played with freedom and truly expressed the player I am.“A first-class debut at 16, more than 200 games, over 500 wickets, a One Day Cup and a Championship win - it’s been a pretty good go. I can appreciate those accomplishments more than ever now and, perhaps for the first time, give myself the self-validation I deserve.”Gloucestershire director of cricket Jon Lewis called Miles' decision brave and said the club would fully support him as he moves away from professional cricket.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mukesh Kumar, Akash Deep blow J&K away as RoI win Irani Cup
articles.summary: The defining moment of the Irani Cup clash between Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir and Rest of India came on Sunday at the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium.
articles.body: The defining moment of the Irani Cup clash between Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir and Rest of India came on Sunday at the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium.Chasing 279, J&K were 65/2 when Bengal pacer Mukesh Kumar urged stand-in RoI captain Sarfaraz Khan — regular skipper Rishabh Pant was on the sidelines with fever — to give him one more over. Mukesh made it count.In the 13th over, he trapped Shubham Pundir lbw for 9 with a delivery that jagged back in, with Sarfaraz taking a successful review after the umpire had ruled it not out. He then bowled J&K captain Paras Dogra, their first-innings top-scorer with 75, with a sharp delivery that crashed into middle stump after Dogra played inside the line.That double blow broke the chase. With Mukesh and Akash Deep operating at full tilt, RoI bowled J&K out for 111 in 28.4 overs to complete a thumping 167-run win and claim the Irani Cup for the 33rd time — their first title since the 2023-24 season.Mukesh was outstanding, finishing with 6/33 in 10.4 overs. Akash Deep, returning from a seven-month injury lay-off, was equally incisive, taking 3/25 in nine overs. The two India pacers shared nine wickets as J&K collapsed from 54/0, losing 10-57.For Mukesh, match figures of 8/121 on a seaming surface were a timely reminder to the national selectors of his ability to exploit helpful conditions, especially with India’s New Zealand tour ahead. Akash Deep, too, strengthened his case, finishing with match figures of 6/78 after taking 3/43 in the first innings.Pant, though unable to field due to illness, appeared pleased while lifting the trophy — a fitting birthday gift on the day he turned 29. There’s also a possibility that he could miss Delhi’s Ranji opener vs Bengal on Oct 11.J&K had begun brightly through openers Shubham Khajuria (36) and Qamran Iqbal (32), who added 54 runs off 61 balls. Akash broke the stand by trapping Iqbal lbw before Mukesh’s burst changed the game.Mukesh later had wicket-keeper Kanhaiya Wadhawan caught behind for 2 and then cleaned up the tail in the 29th over, removing Abid Mushtaq, Umar Nazir and Sunil Kumar to finish the job.The third seamer, Mukesh Choudhary, also had a strong match, taking 5/47 in the first innings and six wickets overall.RoI’s biggest match-winner, however, was Ravichandran Smaran. The No. 6 batter was rightly named Player of the Match for his superb knocks of 68 and 135, the second innings century proving decisive in setting up the win.Earlier, RoI, resuming on 306/8, were bowled out for 319. Smaran, the last man dismissed, fell to Sunil Kumar, who finished with 3/56.J&K, who missed swing bowler Auqib Nabi, will need to regroup quickly before beginning their Ranji Trophy title defence against Madhya Pradesh at home from Oct 11.Brief scores: Rest of India 237 and 319 (R Smaran 135; S Kumar 3-56) beat Jammu & Kashmir 278 and 111 (S Khajuria 36, Mukesh Kumar 6-33) by 167 runs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: A bizarre moment during the Canada's premier T10 cricket league semi-final between Toronto Sixers and Mississauga Masters left players, commentators and
articles.body: A bizarre moment during the Canada's premier T10 cricket league semi-final between Toronto Sixers and Mississauga Masters left players, commentators and fans surprised.A delivery from USA pacer Ali Khan flew over the batter and wicketkeeper before landing in the stands, but Toronto were awarded only five runs instead of six.Toronto had posted 130/4 in 10 overs, with Kieron Pollard smashing 40 from 16 balls. During the ninth over, Khan bowled a bouncer that went over Pollard and the wicketkeeper before clearing the boundary without touching the bat.The commentators initially thought it would be a wide and six. However, the umpire awarded five runs to Toronto. Under MCC laws, a six can only be given when the ball has been hit by the bat.Watch:According to Law 19.7, if a ball crosses the boundary without being struck by the bat, it is treated as a boundary four. Since the delivery was also a wide, the additional one-run wide penalty is added, making it five runs in total.Toronto reach finalDespite the unusual incident, Toronto Sixers went on to beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and secure their place in the final. Mississauga put up a strong chase, led by Alex Lees, who smashed 39 off just 11 balls, but they could not complete the chase.In the other semi-final, Vancouver Anchors defeated Brampton Blitz by six wickets. articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has opened up about his conversations with teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and explained why the youngster had to wait for his chance despite being in good form.Sooryavanshi made history earlier this year when he became the youngest Indian to play international cricket. He made his T20I debut against England at the age of 15 years and 99 days, breaking Sachin Tendulkar’s long-standing record.He then became the youngest player to score a half-century in men’s international cricket when he reached the milestone against Zimbabwe at 15 years and 118 days.Gambhir explains Sooryavanshi’s waitDespite his early success, Sooryavanshi did not get a game during the entire Afghanistan series or the one-off T20I against Japan ahead of the Asian Games.The 15-year-old returned to the India XI in the Asian Games semifinal against Sri Lanka. He made a bigger contribution in the game, scoring 38 off 21 balls.Gambhir said he had explained to Sooryavanshi that being in good form does not always mean a player will immediately get an opportunity."It was a new experience for me as well. Yes, he was in good form, but I made him understand that sometimes, because of the players who have done well for a long time, he will have to wait for his opportunity. And there's one more thing, social media or outside noise doesn't decide the playing eleven," Gambhir said on JioStar.‘We can't suddenly ignore a combination’Gambhir said the playing XI is picked based on what the coach and captain believe is the best combination to win a match."It depends on who in that dressing room, or who the coach and captain feel can win us the match, or what is the best playing eleven, and who have done well for such a long time. articles.body: MUMBAI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has deputed a three-member selection committee, headed by former India seamer Harvinder Singh and including ex-first-class cricketers Sridharan Sharath (Tamil Nadu) and Amitabh Vijayvargiya (Madhya Pradesh), to Bihar to pick the squad for the upcoming Ranji Trophy, which will kick off on October 11, TOI has learnt.Harvinder and Sharath, who was also the junior chief selector, have been senior national selectors in the past.To pick Bihar's junior teams for the BCCI's various age-group tournaments — Under-16, Under-19 and Under-23 — the BCCI has formed a three-member selection committee comprising ex-national junior selector Harvinder Singh Sodhi, former Punjab allrounder Krishan Mohan and former Gujarat wicketkeeper Pathik Patel.“All the selectors have reached Patna today and begun their work of identifying talented local cricketers at the Moin-Ul-Haq Stadium in Patna,” a source tracking developments said.On September 16, the Supreme Court appointed former Patna High Court judge Justice Ashwani Kumar Singh as the administrator of the Bihar Cricket Association (BCA).Before the last season too, the BCCI had appointed a four-member selection committee to pick various age-group teams for the Board's tournaments.That committee included former India chief selector Chetan Sharma, Harvinder Singh, ex-India pacer Salil Ankola, and former India women's team left-arm spinner and national chief selector Neetu David.Promoted to the Elite Group, Bihar will take on Uttar Pradesh in their Ranji Trophy opener at Rajgir. articles.title: India tour of New Zealand: Exposure for Test regulars to highlight selection meeting
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The India men's senior selection committee is likely to meet in the next 48 hours to pick the four squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The India men's senior selection committee is likely to meet in the next 48 hours to pick the four squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. The meeting, which interim chief selector Pragyan Ojha is set to chair, was postponed from Monday because of Prasidh Krishna's pending fitness reports. The four selectors will soon get into a huddle to pick the T20I, ODI, Test and India A squads for the tour, which begins with the shortest format on October 22.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that since the A series, starting from October 24, overlaps with the T20Is and ODIs, the selectors are delicately handling the availability and exposure situation. While they don't want to dilute the two squads, providing red-ball exposure for Test regulars will be the top priority when they meet.Some India A bowlers might also stay back to assist the Test team with preparations. Spinners Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Vipraj Nigam and Shivang Kumar accompanied the Test team in Sri Lanka, and this time around, fast bowlers could well be asked to stay back in New Zealand after their A assignment.After his heroics in the Irani Cup fixture against Jammu & Kashmir, Mukesh Kumar is back on the selectors' radar and is likely to be drafted into the A squad for the three matches. Akash Deep will also be asked to play some games to be absolutely ready for the two Tests. The selectors are also deliberating on Jasprit Bumrah's readiness. As TimesofIndia.com first reported, the management wants the fast bowler to increase his workload before joining the squad for the Wellington Test.The Ojha-led panel will be in a tight spot addressing the Bumrah situation, as asking the bowler to play one of the A fixtures could dilute their ODI attack. The option of a Ranji Trophy fixture was also on the table, but some decision-makers are uncomfortable with making him toil in the domestic circuit.Ishan back in red-ball discussionsIt is understood that selectors have initiated plans to keep Ishan Kishan ready for the longest format. While they wanted him to feature in the A series, the overlapping of ODIs and T20Is could force them to look towards Dhruv Jurel and Kumar Kushagra. Rishabh Pant, who is playing only Tests now, is expected to complete his preparations by playing at least one A game.The left-hander will not be the only Test regular to do so, as KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan are all expected to feature in at least one fixture. Since KL will be part of the ODI squad, there is a strong possibility of him playing the first fixture from October 24 before joining the ODI squad in Auckland.How many spinners?Saransh Jain is unlikely to be considered with Washington Sundar back to full fitness, but the big question remains: how many spinners will the team carry? Ravindra Jadeja is expected to retain his spot in the playing XI, leaving the thinktank with the options of Manav Suthar and Kuldeep Yadav. It is unlikely that all four will board the flight, and the axe could fall on Kuldeep, considering the team's batting focus.More than a lot of spin-bowling all-rounders, it will make more sense to have someone like Nitish Kumar Reddy in the set-up, and there is a strong possibility of the management swaying his way.Too many quicks!Indian selectors will have a happy headache regarding the fast-bowling combination for the Tests. If all are fit and available, the onus will be on the selectors to choose the best-suited options from Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Akash Deep and Auqib Nabi. The scales, for now, heavily favour the first four, but an injury could open the door for either Nabi or Mukesh Kumar.ODI depthThe ODI depth will also be tested, as the Test regulars are likely to leave the squad for at least one fixture, if not both. Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Dhruv Jurel and Nitish Kumar Reddy could all be unavailable, which will force the selectors to reward consistent performers in the domestic and A circuits.Ruturaj Gaikwad, Kushagra and Naman Dhir will remain in the mix. Also watch out for Mayank Yadav, as he has been making a strong case for himself with his improved workload and ability to maintain his pace in long spells.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Coach and captain want to give longer rope to certain players': KL Rahul reveals India's 2027 World Cup plans
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India batter KL Rahul says he is working on improving his game against the old ball so that he can help the team score more runs in the middle
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India batter KL Rahul says he is working on improving his game against the old ball so that he can help the team score more runs in the middle overs.Rahul spoke to JioStar after scoring 129 off 87 balls in the third ODI against West Indies. India posted 351, but the total was not enough as the visitors chased it down in 48.2 overs.India had already won the series after taking the first two games.Rahul said batting in the final 10 overs becomes difficult when the ball gets old and starts to reverse swing."It's not been easy to get 80-90 in the last 10 overs. The ball's been getting reverse swing, and even in this game, once the ball got old and soft, and started to reverse swing, as a batter you don't feel confident enough to take on the long-on and deep mid-wicket fielder if it's a big boundary on that side," he said.‘Trying to play with softer, older balls’Rahul said he is now working on finding ways to attack the older ball, especially because he naturally prefers facing a harder ball."...I like the hard ball coming onto me, I can use the pace. So that's something I've been working on, trying to play with softer, older balls and being able to hit sixes with that."I constantly try to get better within my own game, understand my role, understand what a number five and number six batter has to do to consistently put up performances for the team," he added.India want to push towards 370-380Rahul also spoke about India’s preparations for the ODI World Cup in South Africa next year.With teams regularly chasing big totals, Rahul said 340 or 350 is no longer always a safe score. He believes India’s middle order must find ways to score faster and push the team towards 370 or 380.West Indies chased 352 in 48.2 overs in the third ODI. India had also chased a record 406 in the second ODI in Guwahati, completing the chase in just 43.2 overs."We don't want to go too far away from the plan but also experiment a little bit as a batting unit. The goal so far has been about can we score 330-340 while batting first, but we're seeing that 340s and 350s get chased down very easily in one-day cricket," he said."So how can batters, once set, keep pressing on and get 370s and 380s, or push for 400 on a given day. The minute we as middle-order batters go in, the aim is to ensure that we do not take too much time to get going and start rotating the strike and keep hitting a boundary every six or seven balls."The coach and captain have been very clear on the personnel they want to bring in. They want to give a longer rope to certain players who we feel might be important for the World Cup," he explained.Rahul wanted more time in the middleRahul has been batting at No. 5 or No. 6 for some time. He said his 129 against West Indies was important because it allowed him to spend a long time at the crease and test the changes he has been making to his batting."I wanted to spend more time with the bat out there in the middle and the last time I really got to bat for a long duration in ODI cricket, in the middle-order was in early January this year against New Zealand, and since then I haven't really got a lot of time to play a long innings."And next year is a big one, with the World Cup starting in October, so it's important for me to get valuable batting time because off the field I'm trying a few things and I want to test that in the game."And only then will you know whether the work that you're putting behind the scenes is working or not, or what I need to do differently. So yeah, it was important for me to get some batting time," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs WI: Why India and West Indies were fined after 3rd ODI
articles.summary: India and the West Indies have been fined for maintaining slow over-rates during the third and final ODI of their three-match series in New Chandigarh on
articles.body: India and the West Indies have been fined for maintaining slow over-rates during the third and final ODI of their three-match series in New Chandigarh on Saturday.India were four overs behind the required rate after time allowances were taken into account, while the West Indies were two overs short. As a result, India were fined 20 per cent of their match fee, while the West Indies received a 10 per cent fine."In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement.Both captains accepted the charges and the proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.The penalties were imposed by Prakash Bhatt of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees.On-field umpires Jayaraman Madanagopal and Sam Nogajski, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Virender Sharma had levelled the charges.West Indies end ODI series on a highThe West Indies had already lost the three-match series 2-0 before the final ODI, but they finished the series with a memorable win.Led by an unbeaten 162 from captain Shai Hope, the visitors successfully chased down 352, recording their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket. Their previous best was 331/5 against Ireland in 2019.Hope also created history with his innings. He became the first wicketkeeper-captain to score more than 150 runs in an ODI innings.His knock was also the highest score by a West Indies men's batter in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Brian Lara's 153 against Pakistan in Sharjah in 1993.With the ODI series now over, India and the West Indies will shift their focus to the five-match T20I series, which begins on Tuesday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
