articles.title: England confirm 50-over warm-up fixture at the Waca before Australia tour
articles.summary: England confirm warm-up fixture at the Waca before this winter's white-ball tour of Australia - a stark contrast to last year's Ashes defeat.
articles.body:
England have "learned" from the mistakes of their Ashes defeat in booking a 50-over warm-up before their white-ball tour of Australia this winter, says England and Wales Cricket Board chair Richard Thompson.

Brendon McCullum's white-ball side will play a Western Australia XI at the Waca in Perth on 7 November, six days before their one-day international series begins.

The Test team were heavily criticised for only having one in-house warm-up before last winter's dismal 4-1 Ashes defeat.

"There is a lot that was learned," said Thompson.

"You have to remember these decisions are taken so far ahead.

"The reality is in those decisions, mistakes were made and we've corrected that now."

McCullum, who has since been sacked as Test coach but remains in charge of the white-ball sides, admitted during the Ashes that mistakes may have been made with preparation.

Their warm-up was played against the Lions at club ground Lilac Hill, where conditions where vastly different to the first-Test venue, Optus Stadium.

There, England lost inside two days en route to conceding the series at the earliest opportunity.

At the time, the ECB said it had been told the Waca was unavailable.

England are also due to play warm-ups before their Test tours of South Africa and Bangladesh this winter, and before the one-off 150th anniversary Test against Australia in Melbourne in March. Those fixtures were in place before McCullum was replaced by Stephen Fleming as Test coach this summer.

Since the Ashes, the ECB and Cricket Australia have also agreed a reciprocal arrangement that would mean touring teams are provided with better preparation before Ashes series.

"These things are codified and in an agreement, so we're not relying on goodwill," said Thompson, speaking at an event at Lord's to launch a new initiative to boost participation in state schools.

"It can't be a situation where a board chair or CEO move on and the goodwill falls away.

"It's important the Ashes has the best prep for both teams, the best wickets and the best facilities.

"That's something you will see going forward for both teams."

England are learning - these are the World Cup issues they need to solve

England avoid Australia & India in World Cup draw

This addition to England's 50-over schedule is partly a result of that agreement but also comes after McCullum spoke of a wish to arrange such fixtures to get players "up to speed" before next year's 50-over World Cup.

White-ball warm-up matches have faded from tours in recent years - England have not played one for six years - and, while England have won three 50-over series in a row on the back of a poor run in the format, Joe Root was the only player in their most recent XI with over 50 caps.

They have a minimum of 20 official fixtures before the World Cup next autumn.

"Aside from Jos, Joe and Adil Rashid, there's not a lot of experience in that side," McCullum said after victory over Sri Lanka.

"We're going to try and put on a smattering of warm-up games to try and get guys up to speed as quickly as we can."

England play three ODIs and five T20s in Australia this winter from 13 November to 2 December.

They also play a 50-over tri-series in Pakistan against the hosts and Sri Lanka later this month.

The announcement of England's new batch of central contracts, meanwhile, is expected to come next week, having initially been anticipated at the start of October.

articles.title: 'Same thing could happen at 2027 World Cup': Dinesh Karthik hails Rohit Sharma's measured 92 vs West Indies
articles.summary: Rohit Sharma may have missed out on a deserved century in the third ODI against the West Indies, but his 92-run knock once again underlined why experience
articles.body: Rohit Sharma may have missed out on a deserved century in the third ODI against the West Indies, but his 92-run knock once again underlined why experience could be one of India’s biggest assets heading into the 2027 ODI World Cup.With India rocked by the early dismissals of captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli, Rohit resisted the temptation to attack and instead absorbed the pressure before switching gears later in his innings. His measured approach drew high praise from former India wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik, who believes the knock showed exactly why Rohit will remain crucial for India in South Africa.Rohit absorbs pressure before turning on the heatIndia were in trouble early in the third ODI at the CA International Cricket Stadium in New Chandigarh, losing Gill and Kohli inside the opening three overs. With the pitch offering assistance to the West Indies pacers, Rohit had to put his natural attacking instincts aside.He joined Ruturaj Gaikwad to steady the innings and took his time against a disciplined West Indies attack. Rohit scored just 20 runs from his first 40 balls before accelerating dramatically, eventually finishing with 92 off 85 deliveries. Karthik highlighted that innings progression as the perfect example of how experience allows a batter to assess the situation rather than panic."The beauty of having experience is that they have seen this situation a lot before. If you take Rohit Sharma, when he saw the two early wickets fall, if you see he was on 20 for the first 40 balls with a 50 strike rate. That was because he knew he could trust himself and back it up and get those runs quickly,'' Karthik said on Cricbuzz."And then you see how quickly he moved to 92 after scoring less than a run-a-ball. His strike rate went above 100, but he made that all up in the next 40 balls. In the first 40 balls, he took time, didn't allow wickets to fall and then in the next 40 balls, he went and smashed," he added.Karthik sees Rohit's experience as a World Cup weaponRohit’s ability to change gears according to the demands of the situation was particularly impressive given the quality of the West Indies bowling attack. Jayden Seales and Alzarri Joseph kept the pressure on early, forcing the veteran opener to play a more cautious role.Karthik believes that willingness to respect the conditions and wait for the right opportunity is precisely the kind of experience India could need when they travel to South Africa for the 2027 ODI World Cup."He saw Jayden Seales was bowling a good spell; Alzarri (Joseph) was bowling nice and sharp. He took time, waited for them to bowl in his areas and if not, I am happy to defend. To have that courage and conviction in that moment is what experience is. A lot of people would have tried to do a little more than they should because they would fear. A young Rohit Sharma would have made that mistake but today he has a wealth of experience," he added.'Same thing could happen in South Africa'Karthik believes the lessons from the West Indies series could prove valuable when India face challenging conditions in South Africa. He pointed out that Rohit, Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill could all be required to adapt their games depending on the conditions rather than blindly sticking to an aggressive approach."The same thing could have happened even in South Africa, and that's when the experience of a Rohit or Shubman or Virat can come through, where they are able to lower their gears down and say, 'Okay, I am not going to play big for the moment, and I know I can make up later,'" Karthik added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘He will dominate Indian cricket’: Shreyas Iyer’s big call on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi; Abhishek Sharma says ‘he belongs here’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Fresh from their gold-medal-winning Asian Games campaign, Shreyas Iyer and Abhishek Sharma have returned to the home season with their focus
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Fresh from their gold-medal-winning Asian Games campaign, Shreyas Iyer and Abhishek Sharma have returned to the home season with their focus already shifting towards the next generation of Indian cricket. Among the youngest members of the setup, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has attracted plenty of attention — but Iyer believes the teenage sensation is still waiting for his opportunity to make a major impact.As India prepare to begin their five-match T20I series against the West Indies, Iyer opened up about his interactions with Sooryavanshi, revealing that their conversations often go beyond cricket. The India T20I captain said he deliberately tries to understand the teenager away from the sport, where the youngster is more comfortable being himself.‘Very silent, but on the field, very destructive’Speaking on JioStar’s ‘Follow the Blues: Sarpanch Shreyas’, Iyer said he has enjoyed getting to know Sooryavanshi away from the pressures and expectations surrounding his cricket.“I keep interacting with Vaibhav in terms of what he does outside the field, because everyone talks to him about cricket, and we know how talented and gifted as an individual he is. So, just to talk about his lifestyle outside, that interaction, knowing about his family, what he does, what not, that excites him more because he’s more of himself when he talks about it,” Iyer said.The contrast between Sooryavanshi’s personality away from cricket and his aggressive approach with the bat has also caught the captain's attention.“And a very silent guy, but on the field, is very destructive. So, that’s like an irony when you look at him. He’s a very charming, sweet guy to interact with and good to have him around the dressing room,” Iyer added.While Sooryavanshi remains part of the squad, Iyer stressed that the youngster has to wait for his opportunity, with India's established World Cup-winning openers currently ahead of him in the pecking order.“And I know that his time will come, because we have been playing with World Cup-winning openers right now, and they deserve the time out there and he’s still in the 15. So definitely, when his time comes, he is going to dominate Indian cricket,” Iyer said.Abhishek: ‘He belongs here’Abhishek, who was also part of India's Asian Games gold-medal-winning campaign, echoed Iyer's belief in Sooryavanshi's potential while emphasising the importance of making the teenager comfortable inside the dressing room.The left-handed opener said Sooryavanshi is already more accustomed to the demands of professional cricket than most teenagers his age, having spent several years in the cricket system.“He is a very smart guy. He is not like how we used to behave at 15 or anyone does because he has already been in that cricket setup for 2-3 years. So he knows what, where, and how much to practice. I feel gradually these are things he will learn more with experience. And what we discuss in the team with each other, all teammates, is how we can make him more comfortable,” Abhishek told JioStar.The 26-year-old also believes the responsibility lies with the senior players to ensure that Sooryavanshi does not feel overwhelmed by the attention surrounding his rapid rise.“Because we all know what he has achieved and that he belongs here. So I also feel like it’s my duty as well, to make him feel that all of us, his elder brothers, are here for him. You just have to enjoy and just give your best and win the games whenever you get the chance,” he added.Iyer wants winning to come firstWhile the emergence of youngsters such as Sooryavanshi offers India an opportunity to build depth, Iyer made it clear that experimentation will not come at the cost of results.“The most important thing for me is to win the series, and then we can experiment with the playing combination. Experimenting from the start doesn’t make sense because then the players also get insecure, and then they start questioning themselves, questioning others around the dressing room. And then they go in that dilemma phase where they feel like, ‘Will I get a match ahead or will I not get one?’ I don’t like that mindset. I’ve been in that mindset in the past, and I know how it feels from inside,” Iyer said.The West Indies series therefore marks the beginning of another phase for India, with the Asian Games gold medal now behind them and the focus shifting towards building a settled, confident side.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Michael Bracewell opts out of New Zeadland central contract, set to pursue BBL opportunity
articles.summary: Michael Bracewell has opted for a change in contract status to keep his white-ball career open to opportunities overseas, with the New Zealand all-rounder
articles.body: Michael Bracewell has opted for a change in contract status to keep his white-ball career open to opportunities overseas, with the New Zealand all-rounder set to move to a casual contract for the 2026-27 season and pursue a stint in the Big Bash League.The 35-year-old remains firmly in New Zealand’s plans despite dropping off the central contract list. Bracewell will join Finn Allen, Mark Chapman, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert among the Blackcaps’ casually contracted players.Bracewell keeps Blackcaps commitment intactBracewell’s decision comes as New Zealand Cricket continues to provide greater flexibility to established white-ball players seeking opportunities in overseas leagues. Despite moving to a casual deal, Bracewell will remain available for New Zealand and is expected to be part of the upcoming five-match T20I series against India."The backing from New Zealand Cricket for me to take this opportunity at this stage of my career means a lot," Bracewell said."As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up. I'm still very much committed to the Blackcaps and can't wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series."Bracewell also has his sights set on New Zealand’s upcoming domestic T20 competition, saying he is eager to feature in the inaugural NZ20 from next summer.Nick Kelly earns first New Zealand contractBracewell’s departure from the central contract list has opened the door for Northern Districts batter Nick Kelly, who has earned his first national contract 11 years after making his first-class debut. The 33-year-old made his international debut in March 2025 and has since represented New Zealand in eight ODIs and seven T20Is. He also captained the side in two T20Is against Bangladesh earlier this year after stepping in for the injured Tom Latham.Kelly arrives on the back of a productive stint with Leicestershire, where he accumulated 950 runs across formats. He also struck his sixth List A century in the One Day Cup final against Middlesex.Rob Walter backs experienced KellyNew Zealand head coach Rob Walter, who worked with Kelly for two seasons at Otago, believes the batter's consistency and experience have finally earned him a place among the country's contracted players."Nick's been a standout performer in domestic cricket for several seasons now and it's testament to his hard work that he's earned this first contract at this stage of his career," Walter said.Walter also pointed to the benefits of introducing players to international cricket later in their careers, particularly when they have already developed a strong understanding of their game."Introducing players like Nick to international cricket a bit later certainly has its advantages in terms of the player knowing their game and being able to trust themselves to perform under pressure," he added.Kelly's experience adds depthKelly has scored three fifties in his last four ODIs, further strengthening his case for a regular role in New Zealand's white-ball setup. Walter believes Kelly’s extensive experience could prove particularly valuable, with the batter having played more than 300 professional matches."Nick stuck his hand up with his performances against Bangladesh and the West Indies in what was at times challenging batting conditions, he has more than 300 professional matches under his belt and is one of the best fielders in the country, so he adds a lot to our contracted group," Walter said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In a first, Uttar Pradesh opt for split captaincy and coaching for upcoming domestic season
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a first, the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) is set to adopt a split captaincy and coaching model for the upcoming domestic season,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a first, the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) is set to adopt a split captaincy and coaching model for the upcoming domestic season, with a separate set of coaches and captains overseeing the red-ball and white-ball teams.Wicketkeeper-batter Aryan Juyal will lead Uttar Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy, whereas Karan Sharma will captain the Vijay Hazare Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy teams, respectively. Similarly, former India spinner and Uttar Pradesh veteran Gyanendra Pandey will coach the Ranji Trophy team, while India speedster Sudip Tyagi and Arvind Kapoor will be at the helm for the white-ball team.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the UPCA chairman of the senior men's cricket selection committee, Praveen Kumar, suggested the move. It is aimed at bringing greater focus to the distinct demands of the two formats and strengthen Uttar Pradesh's performances across competitions.It is additionally learnt that all is not well with Arvind Kapoor's appointment in the white-ball set-up. Kapoor has been part of the Uttar Pradesh set-up for close to a decade, but the side has not really punched to its potential during this period.At the Annual General Meeting (AGM) held last week, UPCA vice-president Rakesh Mishra proposed that cricketers who have represented Uttar Pradesh more extensively should be considered for the coaching role. Mishra has strongly opposed Kapoor's appointment, pointing out that Kapoor has already served as Uttar Pradesh's coach multiple times.Yash Dayal returnsYash Dayal is set to return to Uttar Pradesh's Ranji Trophy setup, ending a prolonged period away from competitive cricket. He is being included in the Uttar Pradesh Ranji Trophy squad.Apart from Dayal, Kartik Tyagi, who was with the Indian T20I team in Japan for the Asian Games, has also made the cut. Abhinandan Singh, who made his Indian Premier League (IPL) debut for champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), has also earned a maiden first-class call-up.Leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari has also made his comeback after years in the wilderness. Zeeshan Ansari hadn't played a Ranji Trophy match since 2020. Zeeshan made his red-ball comeback after six years against Sri Lanka A at Galle earlier this year. The 26-year-old is currently on the selectors' radar.The 2026-27 Ranji Trophy will kick-start on October 11. articles.title: SA20 celebrates five years as Graeme Smith targets bigger, better Season 5
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Five years after the first ball was bowled at a sold-out Newlands, SA20 has established itself as one of the leading franchise cricket
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five years after the first ball was bowled at a sold-out Newlands, SA20 has established itself as one of the leading franchise cricket competitions, with more than 1.6 million tickets sold, over 500 million television viewers and a social media following that has grown to four million.As the league prepares for its fifth season, which begins on January 17, 2027, SA20 stakeholders, partners and franchises gathered to celebrate the competition's journey and look ahead to another month of high-profile T20 cricket across South Africa.SA20 League Commissioner Graeme Smith described reaching the five-year milestone as a significant achievement, while stressing that the league's growth has been a collective effort involving franchises, players, partners and fans."Reaching five years is a significant milestone for SA20, but it's not one we've reached alone," Smith said. "As we head into Season 5, we carry that same belief with us, and we can't wait to keep building on it together."The first four editions have produced two champions. Sunrisers Eastern Cape have dominated the competition, winning three titles in 2023, 2024 and 2026. MI Cape Town claimed their maiden championship in 2025 after defeating Sunrisers in the final.The fifth season will once again feature several of South Africa's leading players, including David Miller, Kagiso Rabada, Aiden Markram, Lungi Ngidi and Ryan Rickelton. They will be joined by a strong international contingent featuring Jos Buttler, Sunil Narine, Rashid Khan, Phil Salt and Mitchell Marsh.Smith believes the combination of established international stars, Proteas players and emerging South African talent has been central to the league's success."The combination of international stars, Proteas players and South Africa's emerging talent has been one of the defining features of SA20," he said.The Season 5 squad lists will be completed at the Player Auction in Johannesburg on October 7. Nineteen player slots remain available, with a maximum of $2.10 million to be spent among the four teams participating in the auction. Durban's Super Giants and Paarl Royals have already completed their 19-player squads and will not take part.The new season will begin at St George's Park in Gqeberha on January 17, with defending champions Sunrisers Eastern Cape hosting Pretoria Capitals in a repeat of last season's final.Smith said SA20 would continue to focus on innovation and enhancing the spectator experience as it enters its fifth year."As we enter our fifth season, we are excited to continue building on the legacy and introducing new innovations that will deliver memorable spectator experiences," he said.Tickets for Season 5 will go on sale on November 5.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England to play warm-up in Australia before November series after criticism for lack of preparation ahead of Ashes
articles.summary: England to take on a Western Australia XI in Perth on November 7, six days before first ODI against Australia; Sky Sports' Michael Atherton pleased by Mason Crane's recall for ODI tri-series in Pakistan, says Glamorgan star is better leg-spinning option than the dropped Rehan Ahmed
articles.body:
England's sole Test match warm-up before being thrashed 4-1 was an intra-squad fixture held at club ground Lilac Hill, which in no way replicated the bouncy conditions they ultimately came up against in the series opener in Perth, a contest they lost inside two days.

White-ball coach Brendon McCullum, who was in charge of the Test side during the Ashes thrashing, had said last month that he was hoping to arrange some warm-up games this time around and his team will now take on the Western Australia XI on November 7.

The first one-day international against Australia on November 13 is also in Perth, at Optus Stadium, followed by matches in Adelaide on November 15 and Hobart on November 18.

McCullum's side will then meet their hosts in five T20 internationals, across Melbourne, Carrara, Brisbane, Sydney and Canberra.

England are yet to name their squads for the tour but hope Jacob Bethell will be fit to return having missed the back end of the home summer following a knee injury and subsequent surgery.

Before that assignment, they will play an ODI tri-series in Pakistan, also featuring Sri Lanka, from October 20.

Glamorgan leg-spinner Mason Crane has been called up , in place of the dropped Rehan Ahmed, and is eyeing a first international appearance since the 2017-18 Ashes.

Crane recorded bowling figures of 1-193 from 48 overs on a trying red-ball debut in Sydney back then but has enjoyed a fine season domestically in 2026, playing all 14 County Championship games and backing up his 34 wickets with two hundreds.

The former Hampshire bowler also claimed 15 Vitality Blast wickets.

Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast , former England captain Michael Atherton said: "Crane's call-up is a great story.

"He had a hellish introduction to Test cricket but I thought he showed a lot of character in that game and didn't bowl as badly as his figures suggested.

"He has reaped the benefit of both a bit of experience - he is 29 now and been around the block - and being at a county where he is getting plenty of game time.

"His batting has come on as well which is not going to harm his chances at all.

"I am happy England have moved on from Ahmed from a spin-bowling side as I feel there are better leg-spinners than him.

"To my mind, Ahmed is principally a batter first who bowls leg-spin whereas I see Crane the other way.

"There is time for Ahmed to come back but England have to work out how they see his role and he does, too.

"Crane is definitely a better leg-spinner than him for me and England may be looking at him for the rest of the winter [with a Test series in Bangladesh in February]."

articles.title: ‘Even if he’s not getting game time, he’s still in the dugout’: Morne Morkel’s big message for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel believes teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi can benefit immensely from spending more time around
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel believes teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi can benefit immensely from spending more time around experienced players, even if he does not get a game in the upcoming T20I series against the West Indies.The 15-year-old was part of India's Asian Games gold-medal winning squad and played all the matches in Nagoya, though he could not make a significant impact with the bat. With India set to begin their three-match T20I series against the West Indies on Tuesday, Morkel stressed that Sooryavanshi's development is not dependent only on getting regular game time.More than just game time"We all know the talent of Vaibhav. The more time he spends in this environment with the quality players, the more time he trains at this standard, will only be great for his cricket," Morkel said at the pre-match press conference.The bowling coach highlighted how much a young player can learn simply by being around senior campaigners and observing their routines."And if he's not getting that game time, he's still on a bus, in the dugout, in the hotel with guys with a lot of experience. With him sharing that sort of dressing room and talking to guys, or just actually watching how the guys go through their processes and how they set up innings, will be key for him," he said.Sooryavanshi's place in India's XI for the series opener remains unclear, with the team management yet to finalise its combination.‘Ask the right questions and observe’Morkel said India's responsibility is to create the right environment for young players, regardless of how much time they spend on the field."If you put guys in the right environment and they can ask the right questions and they can observe. So I always challenge them, and for any young player, if he gets game time or if that game time is a little limited, it's still our job to make sure that these guys learn, they grow, and they ask questions," he said.Sooryavanshi opened alongside Abhishek Sharma during India's Asian Games campaign, but Morkel refused to indicate whether the same combination would be retained against the West Indies."I mean that's the combination (Abhishek and Sooryavanshi at the top) they felt for them at the Asian Games. We'll work out tonight what is the best combination for us going into this series. Will they adapt, will they float, will they make any changes, I quite honestly can't give that answer now," he said.Jet lag adds to selection puzzleThe transition from the Asian Games could also influence India's selection for Tuesday's opener. Several players have only recently returned from Nagoya, leaving the management mindful of fatigue and jet lag."...the red flag or the problem might be, our guys are travelling back after the Asian Games. Some of the guys only arrived a couple of days ago, so jet lag, getting over the journey. Once we are up and running and we get the series going, we are all really looking forward to it," Morkel said.India's immediate goal, he added, remains winning matches while simultaneously expanding the pool of players who can step up when given an opportunity."This group of players have played some exceptional cricket over the last couple of years. The guys who got opportunities came in, and they've done a brilliant job. It will be great for Indian cricket if we keep on growing that pool, keep on giving guys that experience of the taste of what it is to play in an Indian shirt."For Sooryavanshi, Morkel's message was clear: every moment spent around India's experienced players is part of his development — whether it comes on the field or from the bus, dugout or dressing room.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chris Woakes: ECB's Cricket For Teachers initiative gets backing from former England bowler
articles.summary: The ECB's new 'Cricket For Teachers' programme and 'Secondary Countdown Cricket' competition are part of the body's ambition to reach more than half of all state secondary schools by the end of 2028,  taking cricket to more than 3,500 teachers and over 1,700 schools
articles.body:
The new 'Cricket For Teachers' programme and 'Secondary Countdown Cricket' competition support the ECB's ambition to reach more than half of all state secondary schools by the end of 2028

Cricket For Teachers is a free teacher training programme designed to give PE teachers the confidence, skills and knowledge to deliver quality cricket sessions for students of all abilities.

Participating schools will receive training, resources, equipment and ongoing support to help establish a sustainable cricket culture at the school.

Woakes, a two-time World Cup winner with England, capped 217 across all formats, said: "I was fortunate enough to discover my love of cricket through opportunities at school and in my local community, and I know how important those experiences can be for young people."

Woakes, who retired from international cricket in 2025, added: "These programmes will help introduce cricket to many more children who may never have picked up a bat and ball before. The more opportunities we can provide in state schools, the stronger and more inclusive the future of our game will be."

Alongside the ECB's new training programme, Secondary Countdown Cricket is a new mass-participation soft ball competition for students aged 11 to 16.

Funding will provide schools with training, equipment, resources and competitive playing opportunities designed to make cricket more accessible than ever before.

Richard Thompson, ECB chair, said: "When we launched the State School Action Plan, we made a commitment to create more opportunities for young people from every background to experience cricket. Today's launch is an important step in delivering that commitment.

"State schools educate the vast majority of young people in England and Wales, so if we are serious about making cricket the most inclusive team sport in the country, we must ensure those schools have the support they need.

"Cricket For Teachers and Secondary Countdown Cricket will help remove barriers, build confidence among teachers and give hundreds of thousands more young people the opportunity to enjoy everything our sport has to offer."

articles.title: No apology, no handshakes from Indian players: Is this why PCB denied NOCs for WCL 3? Pakistan Champions pull out
articles.summary: Pakistan Champions have withdrawn from the ongoing World Championship of Legends (WCL) Season 3 after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) refused to issue
articles.body: Pakistan Champions have withdrawn from the ongoing World Championship of Legends (WCL) Season 3 after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) refused to issue the required No-Objection Certificates (NOCs) to their players, bringing an end to the uncertainty surrounding their participation.The withdrawal comes amid a standoff over conditions reportedly put forward by the PCB in connection with last year's controversial India-Pakistan fixtures.As per a PTI report, the board wanted assurances that Indian players would apologise for refusing to play against Pakistan in the 2025 edition and would be willing to shake hands with their Pakistani counterparts. The WCL management rejected those demands, leaving the NOC issue unresolved.PCB-WCL standoff ends Pakistan's campaignPakistan Champions owner Kamil Khan had been in discussions with the PCB and had requested the board to reconsider its decision. However, the board ultimately maintained its refusal to issue the NOCs."Pakistan Champions regret to confirm that the team will not be able to participate in the ongoing World Championship of Legends (WCL), following the Pakistan Cricket Board's decision to uphold its refusal to issue the required NOC," the team said in a statement on Monday."We respect PCB's authority and its decision, while naturally being disappointed that our players will not have the opportunity to represent Pakistan Champions at this global gathering of cricketing legends. We sincerely thank our players, supporters and fans for their patience, understanding and continued support," it added.According to reports, the PCB had agreed to issue the NOCs subject to certain conditions. These included a written apology from Indian players over their decision to not play Pakistan last season and an assurance regarding handshakes between the two sides. The WCL reportedly accepted the commercial conditions put forward by the PCB but rejected the demands relating to the apology and handshake.India vs Pakistan match called offThe dispute goes back to the 2025 WCL, when India Champions declined to play their scheduled matches against Pakistan Champions amid heightened political tensions. The group-stage match was cancelled, while India again refused to take the field against Pakistan in the semifinal, allowing Pakistan to advance to the final.The PCB subsequently imposed restrictions on the participation of its players in the WCL.The fallout has now also led to the cancellation of the scheduled India-Pakistan clash on October 10 in Season 3. The WCL confirmed that Pakistan Champions would not participate, saying: "Official Update: Pakistan Champions will not be participating in WCL Season 3 due to unforeseen circumstances. WCL Season 3 continues with six teams. The game is still on. The legends continue."Pakistan Champions had finished runners-up in both previous editions, losing to India Champions in the inaugural 2024 final and South Africa Champions in the 2025 final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ECB will 'look at' funding West Indies Test if required, says Richard Thompson
articles.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) will “look at” the unusual step of funding a women’s Test in the West Indies next year in order to aid England’s Ashes preparations.
articles.body:
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) would "look at" the unusual step of funding a women's Test in the West Indies next year in order to aid England's Ashes preparations.

The Test in the Caribbean, part of a multi-format series in the spring of 2027, was announced in 2024 and is scheduled before England's bid to regain the Ashes from Australia.

Last week, Cricket West Indies (CWI) announced a wide range of money-saving measures, including cuts to player contracts.

In March, a women's Test that West Indies were due to host against Australia was cancelled, though the white-ball element of that tour went ahead.

There have been no discussions between the ECB and CWI about cancelling the Test.

The tour as a whole – including three T20s and three one-day internationals in April and May of next year – is not under threat, though exact dates and venues are still to be confirmed.

Asked by BBC Sport if the Test was in doubt, ECB chair Richard Thompson said: "I hope not. That's not expected to be cancelled. I hope it will take place."

However, when it was put to Thompson that the ECB may need to provide some funding for the Test to take place, he said his organisation would "look at" the situation should it arise.

Governing bodies usually have reciprocal arrangements for the home board to pick up the logistical expenses of the visiting team, including things like travel and accommodation.

In the West Indies, these can be inflated by the cost of flying West Indies and visiting players between islands. Last week, CWI said it has spent more than $80m on domestic air travel in the past 15 years.

Thompson pointed to a similarly unusual situation when the Zimbabwe men's team played a Test in England last year, with the ECB paying the visitors a touring fee.

"We want that Test match to play out," said Thompson. "It's very important for us because our first women's match in the Ashes is the Headingley Test, so we need a good red-ball warm-up.

"We've got to be playing somewhere and we'd much prefer that to be the West Indies.

"We all have a huge sympathy for the West Indies, we all want to see a successful West Indian nation. They have very unique challenges and I hope through the International Cricket Council and others we can find a way through this."

The first match of the multi-format women's Ashes series is the sole Test at Headingley in June – the only Test, men's or women's, staged north of Nottingham next summer.

England have played one Test since they lost every game on the Ashes tour of Australia in early 2025 – a defeat by India at Lord's earlier this year.

They have not played West Indies in a women's Test since 1979, while West Indies have not played a Test against anyone since a trip to Pakistan in 2004.

The Test in West Indies is one part of England's Ashes Test preparations. In January, the squad will take part in a 10-day red-ball training camp in India.

In 2023, England played Australia A and Australia played England A as Test warm-up matches and that arrangement could be replicated in 2027. Plans for domestic players to potentially be involved in some red-ball cricket in the early part of next season are also being finalised.

Thompson was speaking at Lord's as the ECB launched initiatives to take cricket to more than 1,700 state secondary schools and more than 3,500 teachers.

'Cricket for Teachers' and 'Secondary Countdown Cricket' are part of the ECB's aim to reach half of all state secondary schools in England and Wales by the end of 2028.

Earlier this year, a report by the Sutton Trust found cricket to be one of the most elitist jobs in the country, with 59% of male professionals and 50% of women privately educated.

"We really want teachers to upskill and be able to coach," said Thompson. "The second part is to be able to do something no other team sport can do, which is bring boys and girls together until the age of 16.

"This adds to the pathway. It's another stepping stone for a late developer, or an opportunity for someone to think they want to play the game properly, with a hardball.

"It's meaningful in that we want to reach one and a half million children who have never played the game before. That's a significant programme and the ambition that sits behind this."
